evidence_passages.text: To make `Bun.WebView` connect to an already-running browser over a CDP WebSocket, Bun documents the `backend` object form with `type: "chrome"` and a `url` field set to a `ws://...` DevTools endpoint; the example shown is `ws://127.0.0.1:9222/devtools/browser/abc123...`. The docs say this is how to “Connect to a specific DevTools WebSocket URL.”

claims.text: Bun also documents an auto-connect path: before spawning Chrome, it checks `DevToolsActivePort` in standard profile directories, and if it finds a running browser with remote debugging enabled, it connects over WebSocket instead of spawning a new browser.

claims.text: The explicitly documented lifecycle operations are `view.close()` and `Bun.WebView.closeAll()`.

evidence_passages.text: The explicitly documented lifecycle operations are `view.close()` and `Bun.WebView.closeAll()`.

claims.text: For `view.close()`, the docs say closing is synchronous and idempotent, destroys the page’s renderer process, rejects pending promises on that view with `Error("WebView closed")`, and makes later method calls throw `ERR_INVALID_STATE`. For `Bun.WebView.closeAll()`, the docs say it force-kills the Chrome subprocess and the WebKit host subprocess with `SIGKILL`, causes pending promises on every view to reject on the next event-loop tick, allows later `new Bun.WebView()` calls to respawn browsers as needed, and Bun calls `closeAll()` automatically at process exit.
